title: MiuCam iOS and Android physical-device smoke matrix

deviceSlots.requirement: Oldest supported physical iPhone, minimum supported iOS
Current non-Pro physical iPhone, latest stable iOS
Physical Android with 3-4 GB RAM, oldest supported Android
Current physical Pixel or Samsung class device

cases.title: Camera and microphone demand ownership
setup: Pair one physical server and one physical client on the same LAN.
Keep the native privacy indicators and server diagnostics visible.
steps: Start video-only watch and hold for 30 seconds.
Stop, then start audio-only demand and hold for 30 seconds.
Start video plus audio, then stop the client session.
Open and close local preview with no remote client.

checks.description: Video-only activates camera without microphone privacy indication.
Audio-only activates microphone without camera privacy indication.
Stopping the last demand releases camera, microphone and native audio output.
Local preview remains an independent camera owner and closes cleanly.

cases.title: IPv4 DNS-SD and legacy MJPEG/WAV baseline
setup: Disable IPv6 on the isolated test SSID or use an IPv4-only VLAN.
Launch both devices with the WebRTC pilot disabled.
steps: Discover the server through DNS-SD/NSD and pair without manual IP.
Watch video plus audio for five minutes.
Capture status and latency measurements.

checks.description: Exactly one stable server identity resolves to an IPv4 address.
Selected transport is MJPEG/WAV and both streams remain healthy.
No baseline audio underrun or terminal video failure occurs.

measurements.description: Watch start to audible playout p95.

cases.title: IPv6-only DNS-SD, global or ULA address and WebRTC pilot
setup: Use an isolated IPv6-only SSID with working multicast DNS.
Launch both devices with MIUCAM_WEBRTC_PILOT=true.
steps: Verify DNS-SD returns IPv6 addresses and pair without IPv4 fallback.
Start video plus audio and confirm WebRTC selection.
Capture getStats codec, ICE candidate and latency evidence.

checks.description: All logged URI authorities bracket IPv6 correctly and connect successfully.
DNS-SD stable ID and TXT metadata match the paired server.
The selected LAN ICE pair is IPv6 and does not require TURN.

cases.title: Scoped IPv6 link-local parsing and reachability
setup: Use a two-device LAN where link-local IPv6 is observable.
Record the client-side interface scope name before testing.
steps: Connect through DNS-SD using the resolved scoped address.
Repeat manual entry with [fe80::address%25scope]:port.
Attempt the same literal without a usable client-side scope and record the expected failure.

checks.description: The client-side scope survives parsing and URI creation.
Bracketed percent-escaped manual authority connects to the intended device.
A server-side interface name is never treated as portable evidence on a different client.

cases.title: DNS-SD re-advertise and stable identity
setup: Keep the client discovery screen open while changing server metadata.
steps: Record the initial TXT id, port, protocol and webrtc values.
Restart pairing mode or toggle WebRTC metadata without changing the port.
Restart the server on a different ephemeral test port where supported.
Observe lost/found events and the final client list.

checks.description: TXT id remains stable across re-advertisement and process relaunch.
Port and WebRTC TXT changes appear without restarting the client.
The final discovery list has one unambiguous entry for the device.

measurements.description: Time from server publish to updated client discovery row.

cases.title: Wi-Fi handoff, DHCP change and trusted endpoint rebind
setup: Prepare two APs in the same trusted test LAN or a controllable DHCP lease change.
Start an authenticated watch and alert subscription.
steps: Roam or move the server to the second AP and force an address change.
Wait for DNS-SD to publish the same stable ID at the new endpoint.
Verify video, audio, alerts and controls use the rebound endpoint.
Return to the first AP and repeat.

checks.description: The trusted token and client identity remain unchanged during endpoint rebind.
Status, alerts and subsequent media reconnects use the new address.
No QR scan or manual re-pair is required.

measurements.description: Connectivity-restored to first healthy media p95.

cases.title: iOS background audio and foreground camera lifecycle contract
setup: Use a physical iPhone as the server with active video plus audio demand.
steps: Background the app, lock the screen, then keep the client connected for 60 seconds.
Verify room audio and LAN alerts continue while camera frames pause.
Return to foreground-active and verify camera recovery.
Repeat without microphone demand and inspect the native capability snapshot.

checks.description: Camera pauses in background while active room audio and LAN alerts continue without reconnect churn.
Foreground-active recovery restores camera while preserving the existing audio session.
supportsServerInBackground is true only while server and microphone demand are both active.

cases.title: Android foreground-service lifecycle and process-death contract
setup: Use a physical Android server and grant camera, microphone and notification permissions.
steps: Start media while visible and confirm the foreground-service notification.
Background for two minutes and verify the declared capability snapshot.
Remove the task, then force-stop or kill the process.
Confirm media does not recover invisibly and requires a visible restart.

checks.description: Camera/microphone demand starts only from a visible allowed state.
Foreground service notification accurately reflects active media types.
Process death does not trigger hidden capture recovery.
serviceOwnsMediaHardware/supportsServerInBackground matches observed behavior.

cases.title: iOS audio interruption and route recovery
setup: Start room audio playout and microphone capture on physical iOS hardware.
steps: Trigger an incoming call or CallKit interruption and resume.
Trigger Siri, an alarm and Control Center route changes.
Connect and disconnect wired or Bluetooth audio.
Repeat once while the app transitions background to foreground.
Swap room/client roles and repeat the relevant capture/output interruption path.

checks.description: Native interruption counters and events increment exactly once per transition.
Audio resumes only when the interruption options and app lifecycle allow it.
Route change and media-service reset do not leak or duplicate audio engines.

measurements.description: Allowed interruption end to audible playout p95.

cases.title: Android audio focus, noisy route and recovery
setup: Start room audio playout and microphone capture on physical Android hardware.
steps: Trigger transient focus loss, duck, full focus loss and focus gain.
Disconnect a wired/Bluetooth route to trigger becoming-noisy.
Start another media app, then return focus to MiuCam.
Repeat with the app backgrounded under foreground service.
Swap room/client roles and repeat the relevant capture/output focus path.

checks.description: Native focus counters/events match each injected transition.
Becoming-noisy stops or reroutes output without speaker blast.
Focus recovery does not create duplicate AudioTrack or recorder ownership.

measurements.description: Focus gain to audible playout p95.

cases.title: Thermal governor downgrade and stable recovery
setup: Use a release/profile build, disable external cooling and start video plus audio.
Capture deviceResources, resourceGovernor and media profile every five seconds.
steps: Apply repeatable CPU/GPU/charging load until serious thermal state is observed.
Continue until critical if safe for the device; stop immediately on OS warning.
Remove load and observe recovery for ten minutes.

checks.description: Serious thermal pressure selects constrained or survival policy.
Critical pressure with audio demand selects audio-first/audio-only behavior.
Recovery upgrades without rapid profile oscillation.
No OS thermal shutdown, crash or unsafe device temperature occurs.

measurements.description: Thermal state change to protective governor state.

cases.title: WebRTC H.264 and Opus codec proof
setup: Enable the WebRTC pilot on both physical devices and allow only one peer.
steps: Start video plus audio and wait for connected peer state.
Capture inbound/outbound RTP codec and selected candidate-pair stats.
Toggle audio demand off and on without replacing the video peer unexpectedly.
Close the session and confirm tracks, peer and capture demand are released.

checks.description: Negotiated video codec is H.264, with payload/profile details recorded.
Negotiated audio codec is Opus.
Exactly one peer is active and close releases all tracks.
Selected candidate pair is LAN host ICE as declared by the pilot.

cases.title: WebRTC negotiation and capacity fallback to MJPEG/WAV
setup: Enable the WebRTC pilot and prepare a second client or a codec-disabled test build.
steps: Occupy the single WebRTC peer, then start a second watch.
Repeat with H.264 or Opus capability unavailable where the device permits.
Observe pilot cleanup, replacement session start and legacy media.

checks.description: Fallback reason identifies capacity, capability or negotiation failure.
Failed pilot session and peer are closed before legacy start.
MJPEG video and WAV audio become healthy without re-pairing.

measurements.description: Pilot failure to first healthy legacy media.

cases.title: Thirty-minute MJPEG/WAV physical soak
setup: Use a profile/release build and capture authenticated /status every five seconds.
steps: Run 15 minutes baseline, five minutes weak network, then ten minutes recovered baseline.
Exercise alerts, audio toggle and one foreground/background cycle.
Record memory after five-minute warm-up and at completion.

checks.description: No crash, OOM, stuck privacy indicator or unreleased socket occurs.
Quality and media recover after weak network without app restart.

measurements.description: Baseline audio underruns per ten minutes.

cases.title: Thirty-minute H.264/Opus pilot soak
setup: Use a profile/release build with WebRTC pilot enabled and one peer.
steps: Run 15 minutes baseline, five minutes weak network, then ten minutes recovered baseline.
Capture getStats every five seconds and perform one Wi-Fi roam.
Close the watch and confirm peer, tracks and native demand return to zero.

checks.description: H.264 and Opus remain negotiated for the complete peer lifetime.
No crash, OOM, peer leak or unexpected legacy fallback occurs.
Closing the watch releases peer, tracks and media demand.

measurements.description: WebRTC video latency p95 over the soak.
